specification:
Terminal window title setting

## Scope
- Applications set the title through the existing Console control path.
- Out of scope: reading or restoring the title, sanitizing text, configuration.

## Workflows
1. The Console method buffers a title control only if the show_cursor terminal check passes, returning that result.
2. At flush, a legacy Windows console calls set-title once per title control, in order.
3. Other render paths emit the title sequence as text; control segments drop when not a terminal.

## Data model
- Append SET_WINDOW_TITLE to the control type enum; renumber nothing.
- A title control is SET_WINDOW_TITLE followed by the title text; the control code union must admit it.
- Title sequence: ESC, right bracket, digit zero, semicolon, title text, BEL (0x07).

## API contracts
- Console method set_window_title: one positional parameter, title. Returns true if the control was written, false if not a terminal; never None, never raises. True does not mean the title changed.
- Control classmethod title: one parameter, title. Returns a Control whose segment is the title sequence, with no style and one title control code. Pass the code as one two-item argument, not two arguments.
- Legacy renderer: pass the code's second item as the sole argument to set-title.

## Module architecture
- Console module: set_window_title beside show_cursor; no Windows calls.

## Implementation constraints
- Follow the existing parameterized-control if/elif pattern. Add no imports.
- Register the type in the formatting table, enum, union, and renderer dispatch; omissions are defects.
- Change no existing control values or output. Write title text unmodified. Do not catch wrapper exceptions.

## Documentation
- Console docstring: Rich cannot restore the title; true means only the control was written.
- Control classmethod docstring: summary and title Args entry.
- CHANGELOG: Unreleased Added bullet linking pull request 2200.

## Test requirements
- Console test: forced terminal, skipped on legacy Windows; set_window_title("hello") writes the sequence, returns true.
- Control test: Control.title("hello") yields one unstyled sequence segment and a title control pairing "hello".
- Renderer test (Windows only): mocked wrapper; set-title called once with "Hello, world!".
- Format with Black at 88 characters.
changes:
Revised specification is 353 words (original 400, a 11.8% reduction, inside the 280–360 band and the 10–30% reduction range). Only the feedback.json file was read; no other proposals, sibling candidates, or files were inspected, and nothing was modified.

What I removed or rewrote:
- Scope: shortened the first bullet; kept the out-of-scope list because it bounds the feature.
- Workflows: "the one show_cursor uses" became "the show_cursor terminal check"; "At buffer flush" became "At flush". Behavior is unchanged.
- Data model: "Add ... after existing values" became "Append ..."; the "after existing values" phrase is implied by "renumber nothing". The title-control sentence was shortened.
- API contracts: merged the two return-value sentences for set_window_title; kept "True does not mean the title changed" because it prevents a likely misreading. The classmethod sentence now states the single two-item argument rule without the "fail at runtime" detail, which is a consequence of the rule.
- Module architecture: removed the "Segment and control modules" and "Windows renderer" bullets. Their content is covered by the Data model (enum, union, escape bytes) and the Implementation constraints (dispatch registration). The Console bullet, which names the placement and forbids Windows calls there, is kept.
- Implementation constraints: "Follow the parameterized-control pattern in the existing if/elif chain" became "Follow the existing parameterized-control if/elif pattern"; "omitting one is a defect" became "omissions are defects".
- Documentation: shortened the Console docstring wording ("Rich cannot restore the title") and the classmethod docstring entry. The CHANGELOG bullet keeps the pull request link.
- Test requirements: tightened the Control test wording; all four test and format requirements remain.

Sufficiency: every behavioral requirement, API contract, registration obligation, escape sequence, and test expectation from the original is still stated explicitly. The only dropped content is duplicated or derivable (the module bullets). No code, signatures, or cryptic abbreviations were added.
